top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, firm heterogeneity and selection in trade) is a single identifiable discovery. Its predictions could have failed and were tested on firm-level data in many countries for over twenty years: only some firms export, exporters differ systematically, and liberalisation reallocates activity within industries. These are not implied by the representative-firm models behind the 2008 prize, so the advance is distinct. Maturity is not in question. A two-name credit follows the structure of the contribution: Melitz (2003) is the origin, and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extends it to exporting versus foreign investment. The main costs are the uncredited precursors (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn) and welfare magnitudes that depend on distributional assumptions. I would handle both with a narrow citation on mechanism, not a welfare number, and an explicit acknowledgement in the scientific background. I do not count the broad agreement among members as merit. No award (P000) is clearly worse, because a well-attributed, mature, empirically confirmed discovery is available.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile for Helpman or Melitz. Disclosed without adjudication: SSE colleagues on the committee, long co-authorship with Magnus Johannesson (former committee member, not a candidate), Institute for Replication and Harvard evolutionary-dynamics ties, none involving the credited names. As a metascience researcher I may weight testability and replication evidence more heavily.
